BiblicalUsage: Se'ar is hair, and it marks two men. Elijah was known by it — a hairy man, girt with a girdle of leather — and when the messengers described him, the king knew at once it was Elijah the Tishbite. Absalom's hair was his weight: he polled it every year, and weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hair tells on both men: Elijah's marked the prophet, and Absalom's marked his pride, and pride is what left him hanging in the oak in the end.
